title: Auto-rollback alert tuning workbook (SRE) — thresholds, false positives, paging policy, post-launch plan
body:
Workbook purpose
- Provide initial threshold proposals for auto-rollback (latency + error) and an explicit tuning plan to reduce false positives after GA.
- Define what pages vs what creates tickets (and when we should do neither).
- Capture early hypotheses on flapping modes (low traffic, cold start, monitor staleness) and how policy knobs mitigate them.

Owner / cadence
- Owner: SRE (Aisha / Rafael)
- Review cadence: weekly for first 4 weeks post-GA; then monthly.
- Inputs: rollbacks-by-cause metrics (ENG-2318), incident-bot events, customer tickets, game day outcomes.

Assumptions / definitions (align w/ Confluence SLO definitions)
- Latency signal: p95 end-to-end request latency measured at Redwood API edge (includes routing + model inference time). Use per-route/model/region/tier series when available; otherwise roll up per route + tier.
- Error signal: 5xx ratio (server errors) over total requests at the same label cardinality.
- Rollback is only evaluated when rollout stage is canary or A/B AND traffic to candidate >= min_traffic AND warmup elapsed.
- Baseline comparison: compare candidate vs current stable (same route/model family/region/tier).

Sheet 1 — Proposed defaults by tier (v0)

Table: Global policy knobs
| knob | proposed default | rationale | notes |
|---|---:|---|---|
| evaluation_window | 5m rolling | faster MTTR while smoothing spikes | consider 10m for Dedicated if too noisy |
| consecutive_breaches_required | 2 | reduce single-window blips | effectively ~10m persistence |
| warmup_grace_period | 10m after traffic>0 | avoid cold caches / JIT / load ramp | requires rollout-controller awareness of “traffic started” |
| min_traffic_rps | 1.0 rps per candidate per region | guardrail for low-volume false positives | revisit for enterprise low-QPS tenants |
| cooldown_after_rollback | 30m | prevent flapping | also blocks repeated auto-actions during correlated incidents |
| must_be_worse_than_baseline | true | avoid rolling back when whole system is degraded | baseline = stable in same scope |
| baseline_delta_floor_latency_ms | 50ms | ignore tiny deltas | for small models where p95 is ~150ms, 50ms may be high; tune per route class |
| baseline_multiplier_latency | 1.25x | simple and explainable | if stable p95=200ms, trigger at >=250ms AND delta>=50ms |
| baseline_multiplier_error | 2.0x | avoid rollback during global incidents | must also exceed absolute error threshold |
| fail_behavior_on_monitor_outage | fail-open (no rollback) + page if prolonged | rollback w/o signal is worse | see Sheet 4 |

Table: Latency thresholds by customer tier (candidate vs baseline)
| tier | latency_stat | trigger condition | absolute guardrail | comments |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Hosted / Self-serve | p95 | candidate_p95 >= max(baseline_p95*1.30, baseline_p95+75ms) for 2 windows | candidate_p95 >= 900ms (regardless baseline) | self-serve tends to be bursty; keep conservative |
| Dedicated | p95 | candidate_p95 >= max(baseline_p95*1.25, baseline_p95+50ms) for 2 windows | candidate_p95 >= 750ms | customers pay for predictability; tighter than Hosted |
| Private (VPC) | p95 | candidate_p95 >= max(baseline_p95*1.25, baseline_p95+75ms) for 2 windows | candidate_p95 >= 1000ms | more heterogenous infra; keep absolute guardrail higher |

Table: Error thresholds by customer tier
| tier | error_stat | trigger condition | absolute guardrail | comments |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Hosted / Self-serve | 5xx_ratio | candidate_5xx >= max(baseline_5xx*2.5, 0.8%) for 2 windows | candidate_5xx >= 2.0% | avoid rollback due to sporadic deploy blips |
| Dedicated | 5xx_ratio | candidate_5xx >= max(baseline_5xx*2.0, 0.5%) for 2 windows | candidate_5xx >= 1.5% | Dedicated should page earlier; also ensure we don’t roll back entire fleet simultaneously |
| Private (VPC) | 5xx_ratio | candidate_5xx >= max(baseline_5xx*2.0, 0.7%) for 2 windows | candidate_5xx >= 2.0% | depends on customer ingress patterns; verify labels |

Notes / open items
- Need to ensure baseline series exists for every scope; if baseline missing -> verdict=UNKNOWN, do not rollback.
- Confirm “baseline_5xx” uses same exclusion filters (timeouts? request cancellations?) as candidate.

Sheet 2 — Route classes (optional overrides)

Motivation
- A single global threshold won’t fit embedding vs chat streaming vs reranking.
- Proposal: allow route_class overrides (for Redwood-managed routes) with a small set of buckets.

Table: Route class proposals
| route_class | examples | latency sensitivity | suggested baseline_multiplier_latency | suggested delta_floor | notes |
|---|---|---|---:|---:|---|
| chat_streaming | /v1/chat/completions (stream) | medium | 1.30x | 75ms | streaming hides tail somewhat; but head-of-line still matters |
| text_nonstream | /v1/completions | high | 1.25x | 50ms | tail is visible directly |
| embeddings | /v1/embeddings | high | 1.20x | 30ms | typically low latency; small regressions matter |
| rerank | /v1/rerank | medium | 1.25x | 50ms | depends on batch sizes |

Guardrail
- If route_class override exists, must still respect absolute latency guardrail for tier.

Sheet 3 — False positive analysis (initial hypotheses + mitigations)

Table: Observed / expected false-positive modes
| category | symptom | why it causes bad rollback | mitigations (policy) | mitigations (eng) | how to detect |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| low traffic | p95 spikes, err ratio jumps due to tiny denominators | one 5xx in 50 reqs looks like 2% | min_traffic_rps, consecutive breaches | add “min_requests_in_window” option | chart req count alongside SLO |
| cold start / warmup | first 5–10 minutes slow | caches not hot, KV cache empty, autoscaling ramp | warmup_grace_period | rollout controller should track “first traffic timestamp”; pre-warm option | compare candidate latency over time since first traffic |
| correlated incident (global) | stable and canary both degrade | auto-rollback doesn’t help, can flap many tenants | must_be_worse_than_baseline | global incident detection; rate limit rollbacks per cluster | dashboard: stable vs candidate overlay |
| monitor staleness | no fresh datapoints but evaluator reads last value | rollback on stale data | verdict UNKNOWN if monitor stale; fail-open | expose monitor freshness metric; alert on stale monitors | “monitor_age_seconds” panel |
| label mismatch | baseline series missing / wrong region label | evaluator compares apples to oranges | require monitor identity contract | migration scripts + validation dashboards | monitor cardinality + label completeness check |
| partial rollout imbalance | canary traffic is not representative | canary routed to one AZ or host subset | min traffic per region, per-AZ optional | routing guardrails (Mina/Ravi) | compare region/AZ mix candidate vs baseline |
| retries / client errors | error ratio inflated by non-5xx issues | rollback when it’s actually 4xx or cancellations | strict definition: 5xx only | ensure metrics exclude 499/canceled; document | panel: breakdown by status code |

Specific note from SUP-18457
- Customer saw “unexpected rollback” on a low-QPS route. Early read: monitor queried at route+tenant scope, but canary got only ~0.2 rps. One short 5xx burst crossed absolute threshold.
- Action: increase min_traffic_rps default to 1.0 and add “min_requests_in_window=300” as optional follow-up if needed.

Sheet 4 — Paging policy (what notifies humans)

Principles
- Auto-rollback is meant to reduce MTTR without paging for every rollback. Page only when action indicates broader risk or uncertain safety.
- Every auto-rollback should emit an audit event + Slack notification (non-paging channel). Paging should be reserved for:
  1) repeated rollbacks (flapping) that suggests systemic issue,
  2) monitor/evaluator failures (blind spots),
  3) Dedicated/Enterprise high-severity routes.

Table: Notification matrix
| event | channel | page? | who | rationale |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| auto_rollback_executed (Hosted/self-serve) | Slack #rollouts-events + ticket | no | oncall gets ticket (business hours triage) | action already mitigated customer impact |
| auto_rollback_executed (Dedicated) | Slack + PagerDuty (sev3) if >N tenants/region | conditional | SRE oncall | Dedicated expects tighter comms; page only if systemic |
| auto_rollback_executed (Private/VPC) | Slack + page (sev3) if customer is “premium SLA” | conditional | SRE + CSM oncall | customer-managed env, rollback may indicate infra misconfig |
| evaluator_verdict=UNKNOWN due to monitor outage >10m | PagerDuty (sev3) | yes | SRE oncall | we’re blind; rollouts should be paused |
| monitor_fetch_errors > 5% for 15m | PagerDuty (sev3) | yes | SRE oncall + telemetry oncall | dependency issue; could prevent rollback |
| rollback_rate_limited triggered | Slack + ticket | no | SRE | indicates protection kicked in; investigate trend |
| repeated rollbacks same route/model in 24h | PagerDuty (sev3) | yes | SRE | likely persistent regression or config issue |

Paging thresholds (initial)
- “Systemic rollback”: >= 3 tenants in same region within 15 minutes OR >= 5 rollbacks total within 30 minutes (any region).
- “Flapping”: same tenant+route rolls back twice within 6 hours.

Runbook links
- Primary: Confluence runbook-auto-rollback-on-slo-breach (pending final)
- Dashboards: rollout-slo-dashboards-and-alerting (Sergio)

Sheet 5 — Post-launch tuning plan (30-day)

Week 0 (launch week)
- Verify observability plumbing:
  - Monitor freshness panels show expected update cadence.
  - Evaluator lag p95 < 30s.
  - Rollback executor emits idempotency keys and shows dedupe behavior in logs.
- Enable auto-rollback only for internal canaries + 1–2 low-risk Hosted tenants.

Week 1
- Collect baseline distributions:
  - candidate_vs_baseline latency multiplier distribution
  - candidate error ratio distribution
  - number of rollbacks and “near misses” (breach once but not twice)
- Tune min_traffic_rps and warmup_grace_period if >20% of breaches occur within first 10 minutes.

Week 2
- Evaluate false positive rate proxy:
  - % of rollbacks where post-rollback stable metrics did NOT improve within 10m (indicates correlated incident or noise)
- If >30%: tighten baseline requirement (increase consecutive breaches to 3) OR increase min_requests_in_window.

Week 3
- Dedicated cohort expansion gating:
  - rollback effectiveness (time-to-mitigation) <= 15m median
  - <5% of rollbacks classified as false positive (manual review)
  - no more than 1 systemic rollback page/week

Week 4
- Establish steady-state defaults and document per-tier overrides.
- Decide if we need burn-rate evaluation for error SLOs (ADR-0148 option) vs fixed thresholds.

Metrics to add / validate (ENG-2318)
- rollouts.auto_rollback.count{tier,region,route_class,cause}
- rollouts.auto_rollback.rate_limited.count
- rollouts.slo_evaluator.verdict{verdict}
- rollouts.slo_evaluator.monitor_age_seconds (p50/p95)
- rollouts.slo_evaluator.query_errors.count
- rollouts.slo_evaluator.evaluation_lag_seconds

Manual review rubric for classifying rollbacks (for first month)
- True positive: rollback followed by measurable improvement (latency/error) in candidate scope AND stable unaffected.
- Likely false positive: stable also degraded similarly OR traffic too low OR monitor stale.
- Unknown: confounded by concurrent incident / deploy / infra event.

Appendix — Example calculations
Example A (Dedicated):
- baseline p95 = 220ms
- baseline_multiplier_latency = 1.25x => 275ms
- delta floor = 50ms => baseline+50 = 270ms
- Trigger threshold = max(275, 270) = 275ms
- Candidate p95 observed 290ms for two 5m windows with >=1 rps -> eligible for rollback.

Example B (Hosted):
- baseline 5xx = 0.1%
- baseline*2.5 = 0.25%
- absolute error threshold = 0.8%
- Candidate 5xx = 0.6% -> NOT a breach under v0 (still below 0.8%), even though worse than baseline.

Questions to resolve (before finalizing defaults)
- Do we want absolute thresholds at all, or only baseline comparison? (SRE leaning: keep absolute guardrails as “oh no” triggers)
- Should we use p99 for any route_class (embeddings)? Might be too noisy.
- How do we handle “no baseline” during first-ever rollout? Current proposal: UNKNOWN (no rollback) + require manual monitoring.
- Should Dedicated page on any rollback, or only systemic? (leaning systemic only to avoid paging fatigue)

Change log
- 2025-01-18: initial draft thresholds and policy knobs
- 2025-01-29: added paging matrix and initial systemic rollback definition
- 2025-02-11: incorporated SUP-18457 low-traffic findings; raised min_traffic_rps to 1.0; clarified fail-open on monitor outage
